P0100.title: Mass air flow (MAF) circuit malfunction
causes: Air leak between the MAF and throttle body

P0101.title: MAF sensor range/performance
causes: Air leak between the MAF and throttle body

P0106.title: MAP sensor range/performance
causes: Cracked or loose MAP sensor vacuum source
Low engine vacuum from a mechanical problem

P0113.title: Intake air temperature (IAT) sensor high input
causes: Unplugged IAT sensor (often built into the MAF on GM)

P0117.title: Engine coolant temp sensor low input

P0118.title: Engine coolant temp sensor high input
causes: Unplugged or failed coolant temp sensor

P0128.title: Coolant temperature below thermostat regulating temperature

P0130.title: O2 sensor circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0131.title: O2 sensor low voltage (bank 1 sensor 1)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0133.title: O2 sensor slow response (bank 1 sensor 1)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0135.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
causes: Failed O2 sensor heater (replace the sensor)

P0137.title: O2 sensor low voltage (bank 1 sensor 2)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0141.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 1 sensor 2)
causes: Failed O2 sensor heater (replace the sensor)

P0150.title: O2 sensor circuit (bank 2 sensor 1)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0154.title: O2 sensor no activity (bank 2 sensor 1)
causes: Engine running too rich or lean

P0155.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 2 sensor 1)
causes: Failed O2 sensor heater (replace the sensor)

P0161.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 2 sensor 2)
causes: Failed O2 sensor heater (replace the sensor)

P0171.title: System too lean (bank 1)
causes: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, PCV hose, brake booster)
Low fuel pressure (weak pump or clogged filter)
Exhaust leak before the O2 sensor

P0174.title: System too lean (bank 2)
causes: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, PCV hose, brake booster)
Low fuel pressure (weak pump or clogged filter)
Exhaust leak before the O2 sensor

P0300.title: Random/multiple cylinder misfire
causes: Worn spark plugs or plug wires

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 1
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 1

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 2
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 2

P0303.title: Cylinder 3 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 3
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 3

P0304.title: Cylinder 4 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 4
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 4

P0305.title: Cylinder 5 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 5
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 5

P0306.title: Cylinder 6 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 6
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 6

P0307.title: Cylinder 7 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 7
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 7

P0308.title: Cylinder 8 misfire
causes: Bad spark plug or plug wire on cylinder 8
Failed ignition coil (swap it to another cylinder to test)
Clogged or leaking injector on cylinder 8

P0325.title: Knock sensor 1 circuit (bank 1)
causes: Corroded knock sensor or wiring harness. On the GM 6.0L/5.3L the sensors sit under the intake manifold in the valley, and water gets in and corrodes them
Real engine knock (low octane fuel, carbon build-up)

P0327.title: Knock sensor 1 circuit low input (bank 1)
causes: Corroded knock sensor or wiring harness. On the GM 6.0L/5.3L the sensors sit under the intake manifold in the valley, and water gets in and corrodes them
Real engine knock (low octane fuel, carbon build-up)

P0332.title: Knock sensor 2 circuit low input (bank 2)
causes: Corroded knock sensor or wiring harness. On the GM 6.0L/5.3L the sensors sit under the intake manifold in the valley, and water gets in and corrodes them
Real engine knock (low octane fuel, carbon build-up)

P0400.title: EGR flow malfunction
causes: Vacuum or wiring issue to the valve

P0420.title: Catalyst efficiency below threshold (bank 1)
causes: Misfire that damaged the converter (fix misfires first)

P0430.title: Catalyst efficiency below threshold (bank 2)
causes: Misfire that damaged the converter (fix misfires first)

P0440.title: EVAP system malfunction
causes: Loose, cracked, or worn gas cap

P0442.title: EVAP system small leak detected
causes: Loose, cracked, or worn gas cap

P0446.title: EVAP vent control circuit
causes: Clogged vent filter or canister (dirt roads, lifted trucks)

P0455.title: EVAP system large leak detected
causes: Gas cap missing or not tight

P0500.title: Vehicle speed sensor malfunction
causes: Failed speed sensor in the transmission or rear diff

P0521.title: Engine oil pressure sensor range/performance
causes: Failed oil pressure sensor (GM 6.0L: behind the intake, leaks often)

P0601.title: Internal control module memory checksum error

P0700.title: Transmission control system malfunction
causes: The transmission computer has its own code: scan it

P0751.title: Shift solenoid A performance or stuck off

P1101.title: MAF sensor out of self-test range (GM)
causes: Air leak in the intake tube
